question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution:
The correct answer is '**plays**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the clause is "**the music**", which is a singular noun.
 
• In the present simple tense, a singular subject takes a verb with **–s/es** in the third person — hence "**plays**".
 
• The sentence is making a general statement about musical theatre, so the present simple tense "**plays**" is appropriate.
 
• Other options: 
 
 
• **play** – plural verb form; incorrect for the singular subject.
 
• **playing** – present participle; not suitable in this grammatical structure.
 
• **played** – past tense; contradicts the general nature of the statement.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *In contrast, in musical theatre an actor's dramatic performance is primary, and the music **plays**__ a lesser role.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Simple Present Tense** is used to state facts or general truths — which applies here.
 
• Always match the verb form to the subject in number (singular/plural) and person.
